ideas.hypothesis: For listed rail operators and rolling-stock lessors, large rolling-stock procurement announcements (lumpy capex) predict lower subsequent abnormal stock returns, and this negative capex-return relation is stronger for firms facing liquidity shocks that force financing via credit-line drawdowns.

ideas.test: Event study and monthly Fama-MacBeth regressions on ~50-100 listed rail operators, lessors and rail conglomerates (US, Europe, Japan) 2000-2019: hand-collect procurement announcements from trade press, merge with CRSP/Compustat or Datastream, include credit-line usage from 10-K/annual reports, and test whether procurement intensity predicts 12-36 month abnormal returns, interacting with drawdown indicators, after liquidity-bias adjustment.
ideas.disconfirming: No significant post-announcement return drift, or a positive relation, and no difference between firms with and without credit-line drawdowns.
